raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When a grammar request waits past `SGLANG_GRAMMAR_MAX_POLL_ITERATIONS`, `GrammarManager.get_ready_grammar_requests` caches `InvalidGrammarObject("Grammar preprocessing timed out")` for that key. `BaseGrammarBackend.get_cached_or_future_value` treats any cached object as a hit, so every later request with the same schema is aborted with `Failed to compile json grammar: Grammar preprocessing timed out` until `/flush_cache` (which needs an idle server) or a restart.

A timeout is not a property of the schema: the poll counter also runs while the compile waits in the shared executor queue, so one burst of load can permanently break a JSON schema or tool definition. This matches the symptom described in #17608, where `/flush_cache` was the workaround.

## Modifications

- Drop the cache write on the timeout path (`grammar_manager.py`). The request is still cancelled and aborted with the same message. Grammars the backend reports invalid are still cached.
- Rank consistency: the removed write ran after the TP all-gather and PP sync of ready/failed indexes, so the cache stays identical on every rank. The PD decode path calls the same `get_ready_grammar_requests`.

**Trade-off.** `Future.cancel()` cannot stop a compile that is already running.
- With xgrammar (default), the compiler cache shares an in-flight compile of the same schema and keeps its result (checked on xgrammar 0.2.7: 4 threads compiling one slow schema cost ~1 compile of CPU vs ~4x for 4 different schemas), so a retry after the compile finishes is cached normally.
- With llguidance, outlines, or framed reasoner grammars, a schema whose compile itself takes longer than the timeout (>= 50 s by default) is now recompiled on every request and can occupy the shared grammar executor under sustained traffic.
- The old negative entry did not bound this either: there is no in-flight dedup, so every request that arrived before the first timeout already submitted its own compile, and any whitespace change produces a new key.
- Per-key in-flight dedup would bound it; I'd do that as a follow-up. Caching the late result from a done-callback is not safe: it would write the cache at different times on different ranks and desync `grammar_queue` indexes.

Not changed here (follow-ups): the timeout abort still returns HTTP 400 (related to #45132); the `except Exception` branch on the ready path still caches unexpected exceptions as invalid.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, control path only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Testing

- `test/registered/unit/constrained/test_grammar_manager.py`: new `test_timeout_does_not_poison_cache` (real `BaseGrammarBackend` cache, executor returning never-completing futures). It fails on the pre-change code and passes after. `test_timeout_aborts_req` drops the assertion that pinned the timeout caching; `test_invalid_grammar_aborts_req` now asserts a real invalid result is still cached (a mutant that stops caching invalid grammars fails it).
- `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/constrained/`: 150 passed (CPU).
- `pre-commit` passes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -323,9 +323,8 @@ def get_ready_grammar_requests(self) -> List[Req]:
 
             assert isinstance(req.grammar, futures.Future) and req.grammar_key
             req.grammar.cancel()
-            self.grammar_backend.set_cache(
-                req.grammar_key, InvalidGrammarObject("Grammar preprocessing timed out")
-            )
+            # Not cached: the poll budget includes executor queueing,
+            # so a timeout does not prove the grammar invalid.
             error_msg = f"Grammar preprocessing timed out: {req.grammar_key=}"
             req.set_finish_with_abort(error_msg)

@@ -607,6 +607,9 @@ def test_invalid_grammar_aborts_req(self):
         self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
         req.set_finish_with_abort.assert_called_once()
         self.assertIn("compile error", req.set_finish_with_abort.call_args[0][0])
+        mgr.grammar_backend.set_cache.assert_called_once_with(
+            ("json", "bad"), invalid_copy
+        )
 
     def test_aborted_req_removed_from_queue(self):
         mgr = self._make_mgr()
@@ -637,11 +640,26 @@ def test_timeout_aborts_req(self):
         self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
         req.set_finish_with_abort.assert_called_once()
         self.assertIn("timed out", req.set_finish_with_abort.call_args[0][0])
-        # Cache should store InvalidGrammarObject for timeout
-        mgr.grammar_backend.set_cache.assert_called_once()
-        cached_key, cached_val = mgr.grammar_backend.set_cache.call_args[0]
-        self.assertEqual(cached_key, ("json", "slow"))
-        self.assertIsInstance(cached_val, InvalidGrammarObject)
+
+    def test_timeout_does_not_poison_cache(self):
+        """A grammar that times out once must not abort later requests with the same schema."""
+        mgr = self._make_mgr()
+        mgr.SGLANG_GRAMMAR_MAX_POLL_ITERATIONS = 1
+        backend = BaseGrammarBackend()
+        # Compiles never finish, so every request for the key times out.
+        backend.executor = MagicMock()
+        backend.executor.submit.side_effect = lambda *args: Future()
+        mgr.grammar_backend = backend
+
+        req1 = _make_req(json_schema="slow", rid="r1")
+        self.assertTrue(mgr.process_req_with_grammar(req1))
+        mgr.get_ready_grammar_requests()
+        req1.set_finish_with_abort.assert_called_once()
+        self.assertIn("timed out", req1.set_finish_with_abort.call_args[0][0])
+
+        req2 = _make_req(json_schema="slow", rid="r2")
+        self.assertTrue(mgr.process_req_with_grammar(req2))
+        req2.set_finish_with_abort.assert_not_called()
 
     def test_pending_future_stays_in_queue(self):
         """Futures that aren't done stay in the queue."""
